PullRequest.Title: Add transient UI for /btw side questions
PullRequest.Body:

`/btw` currently opens another full chat. This change keeps the source transcript and composer in place and presents the side answer in a transient card immediately above the existing composer.

## Reviewer TL;DR

**A normal durable side chat, with a transient presentation.** The provider still owns the conversation, history, model and response. Closing removes only the card; the same backing chat remains recoverable from the session's Side Chats menu. **Open Full Chat** opens that conversation through the normal Sessions navigation path.

The feature defaults off behind `chat.agentSessions.transientSideChat` (`config.chat.agentSessions.transientSideChat` in ExP). Disabled treatment or an unavailable source host uses the existing full-chat open-and-split flow.

**Invariant:** `/btw` must not hide, replace, move, rebind, or restyle the source composer.

Rebased onto `main` at `17c5935aa72`. The history remains four dependency-ordered commits:

| Commit | Purpose | Review focus |
|---|---|---|
| `570205ea0fb` — `chat: refactor: support embedded response widgets` | Generic response-widget options, hidden-input layout, focus-local routing | Existing full-chat behavior stays the default; embedded renderers cannot shadow full surfaces |
| `41d2771964c` — `sessions: refactor: make send lifecycle explicit` | Request IDs, awaited `preserveActiveChat`, close history, provider option boundary | Concurrent and failing sends cannot affect another navigation follow |
| `2faa43c0465` — `sessions: feat: add transient side-chat presentation` | Card, rollout gate, orchestration, all entry points, accessibility and regressions | Presentation ownership, cleanup, error handling, focus and measured layout |
| `301fb9e55a9` — `agentHost: polish: skip side-chat rename round-trip` | Independent latency optimization | Rename reminder suppressed only for `SideChat` origins |

The durable architecture contract is in `src/vs/sessions/SESSIONS.md`, **Transient side questions**.

## Ownership and flow

```text
/btw, response-selection question, or workbench Ask in Side Chat
  -> create a real provider-backed side chat
  -> ISideChatOrchestrationService.prepare(...)
     -> control / no live interactive host: open and split the full side chat
     -> treatment + live host: close with skipHistory, publish transient state
  -> prepared.send(...)
     -> transient: awaited send with preserveActiveChat
     -> full: ordinary foreground send
  -> provider streams into the side-chat model
```

`ITransientSideChatService` stores resource identities, not provider facades. It resolves current session/chat state reactively and revalidates a per-source presentation ID after awaiting close. Replaced questions, deletion, facade replacement, setting disable, final-host disposal and read-only transitions cannot leave a stale live card.

`ISessionsManagementService` owns provider routing and paired send-start/send-end request IDs. `ISessionsService` owns visible navigation. The `background` and `preserveActiveChat` flags never cross the provider boundary; the explicit provider field picker has a compile-time exhaustiveness guard.

Promotion and full-chat fallback verify that the requested destination became active. A late promotion result cannot delete a replacement card.

## Layout and shared widget integration

The variable-height card is an **in-flow child of `ChatInputPart`**, after the floating status-pill lane and before banners/the original composer. It does not use the fixed-height floating lane or inherit that lane's pointer-event behavior.

The nested `ChatWidget` renders response rows only, with no header/footer, follow-ups, pet or go-to-bottom control, and no visible nested composer. It is created lazily; model loads are identity/cancellation guarded; dismissal releases the widget, model reference, listeners and scheduled layout.

`isEmbedded` provides focus-local action routing while excluding the renderer from full-widget discovery. Event-driven consumers use `lastFocusedChatSurface`. Embedded widgets inherit the enclosing surface's Find support, so Cmd/Ctrl+F continues working from the answer. Both Sessions and workbench Agent Host pills explicitly publish persistent-content visibility, including when the input is read-only.

Layout is frame-coalesced and skips unchanged dimensions. Short answers stay compact; long answers are capped at **60% of the source view**, including the fractional header height, divider and outer borders. Scrolling remains inside the answer. Auto routing metadata is hidden only inside transient cards; the ordinary full chat still shows it.

## Failure handling and accessibility

`FailedAndPresented` means a live card owns the send failure. Dismissed or promoting cards decline that ownership, allowing normal caller notification instead of losing the error during promotion. Failure details are retained if promotion itself fails.

The card is a labelled region described by its question and visible status. Announcements are transition-based. Escape dismisses a pending or completed card, but yields to code-editor selections, suggestion UI and hover. From the source input it additionally yields to active requests, dictation, editing and confirmation interactions. Close returns source focus; successful promotion focuses the full-chat destination.

## Review and verification

Opus 5 maximum-reasoning reviews covered Sessions presentation, lifecycle/orchestration, shared workbench behavior and latest-main integration. Findings were fixed and re-reviewed. The OSS run then exposed routing metadata and border-budget regressions; those were fixed, regression-covered, re-reviewed, and the entire live flow was repeated.

Current validation:

- Complete development build via `npm run build-fast`; client type check and changed-file ESLint/Stylelint pass.
- **283 focused Electron tests pass** (2 existing pending), including send/promotion races, read-only pill visibility, real fractional-header/border measurement, metadata scoping, source input, Find and side-chat entry points.
- **44 Agent Host title tests pass**.
- **Ten authenticated, provider-backed Code OSS scenarios pass on the final rebased build**: source context/composer identity and styling; Find from the card; draft preservation; strict height cap; internal wheel scrolling; code-selection Escape; promotion; pending-card dismissal; selected-response questions; and live setting disable/full-chat fallback.
- Measured long-answer geometry: **524.40625px card in an 876px source view**, below the **525.6px cap**, with **1,410px** scroll extent in a **467px** response viewport.

Screenshots, a Playwright trace, assertion results and a 59-second recording were retained with the session's OSS evidence report.

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: Every outgoing side-chat turn synchronously joined the title contribution's async persisted-metadata database lookup before the turn could be sent.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: Side-chat send startup incurred an avoidable serialized database open/metadata read on each turn.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: Side-chat turns now return before the persisted-title metadata lookup and therefore do not block send startup on that database read or add the rename reminder to the turn.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: Before this change, SessionTitleContribution.onOutgoingTurn awaited prepareInstructionForAgent for every outgoing Agent Host turn, and the contribution dispatcher awaits each contribution serially before sending. For an independent side chat, prepareInstructionForAgent reached _readPersistedTitleMetadata, which awaits sessionDataService.tryOpenDatabase and ref.object.getMetadata. The added SideChat-origin guard at line 519 returns before that storage access. blame_base_line attributes the old await to 274239ff17a15514f74288e0f8fb21eaccce599b.

Scenarios.Scenario: Ask a transient side question through /btw, selected-response UI, or the generic side-chat action
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Provider side-chat creation completes first; transient presentation then hides the new chat and synchronously publishes the card state; the provider send is awaited. Embedded model acquisition starts asynchronously from state rendering and is not awaited before the send.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create the provider-backed side chat through Agent Host connection.createChat
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One create call per submitted side question after capability checks; no per-history-item fan-out.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The previous side-chat flow already created one provider-backed side chat before opening and sending it.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must complete before the transient card can be presented or the question sent.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send the side-chat request through the selected sessions provider
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One provider send per submitted side question.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The previous flow also awaited one provider send after creating and opening the side chat.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited by orchestration so failures can be attributed to the card; response streaming continues after provider acceptance according to the provider contract.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve chat-session content for the embedded ChatWidget on a cold model miss
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one resolution per side-chat resource; concurrent callers are coalesced by ChatSessionsService. For the Agent Host provider, createSideChat already retains the model, so the embedded acquisition is normally a cache hit.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Opening the side chat in the prior full-chat flow also acquired the same model; the transient path changes presentation rather than adding an effective cold resolution.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Started without awaiting it, so it is off the send critical path but gates answer rendering.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One active transient state per source chat; practical multiplicity is the number of simultaneously visible source chat groups, with one provider create and one send per question.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Creation, presentation, and send are serialized for one question. Model acquisition may overlap the send; duplicate remote session resolutions are coalesced by ChatSessionsService, and presentation IDs prevent an older concurrent presentation from replacing a newer one.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Agent Host createSideChat calls _retainChatSessionModel before returning, making the subsequent embedded acquireOrLoadSession warm. ChatSessionsService coalesces cold concurrent resolutions and the widget releases its reference on dismissal/replacement.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: orchestration order, provider calls, model-retention cache, and presentation ownership are explicit in the traced code.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact provider latency and the number of concurrently visible groups vary, but no new per-item boundary fan-out or unbounded concurrency was found.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The feature preserves existing provider boundary cardinality, keeps model loading off the send critical path, and bounds presentation state.

Scenarios.Scenario: Render and stream a transient answer card above the source composer
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The source view constructs a lightweight dormant host; the nested ChatWidget is created only when a transient state exists. During streaming, progress updates are handled synchronously and content-height relayout is coalesced to the next animation frame.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Rendering scales with the single side-chat response and its response-part count. Height is capped at 60% of the source view; frame scheduling coalesces multiple content-height events and repeated equal dimensions skip ChatWidget.layout.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Only one scheduled layout refresh may be pending per card. Each source has one current card, and replacement disposes the prior widget/model before loading the next.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Plaintext conversion uses a WeakMap keyed by markdown objects. The embedded model reference is reused while the card lives and released on dismissal; there is no retained cache owned by the widget after disposal.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the layout path and cleanup mechanics; low for any claim of user-visible jank because no unbounded or repeated collection-wide operation was established.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Large tool-heavy answers can still make individual browser layout passes expensive, but the diff includes frame coalescing, a height cap, and unchanged-dimension suppression, so there is insufficient evidence of a regression beyond necessary UI work.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Synchronous geometry work is bounded and coalesced, and widget/model/listener cleanup covers dismissal, replacement, hiding, and disposal.

Scenarios.Scenario: Fallback to the ordinary full side chat when the experiment is disabled or no live source host exists
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The transient eligibility check returns before any close or model work, then openChat activates the side chat, the view splits it to the side, and only then does the provider send run.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send the side-chat request through the sessions provider
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: This is the same create/open/split/send behavior used before the PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited after the destination is confirmed active.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Load the full chat model while opening the destination view when not cached
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one effective resolution per resource after cache and pending-request coalescing.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The old side-chat orchestration opened this same full destination.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Gates display of the full destination transcript but not multiplied by rows or history entries.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Constant work per submitted question, independent of transcript row count at the orchestration layer.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Operations are serialized as show check, open, split, send; no new parallel burst is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Normal ChatService model caching and ChatSessionsService in-flight coalescing apply. Disabled treatment exits before transient close or embedded widget creation.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the fallback branch and active-chat verification are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider/open latency varies by backend, but boundary count and ordering are unchanged from the base flow.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression; the disabled/default path retains prior boundary cardinality and behavior.

Scenarios.Scenario: Dismiss, replace, delete, disable, or promote a transient side question
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Dismissal/removal synchronously drops observable state; the widget cancels pending loads and releases its model, listeners, scheduled frame, and nested ChatWidget. Promotion awaits one normal openChat and then removes only the matching presentation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Open the existing side chat through normal session navigation during promotion
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One open operation per explicit promotion action.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Before transient presentation, the side chat was already opened as part of submission, so no later promotion action existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited before the card is removed so the destination is confirmed active.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Cleanup is linear in the small set of active transient states and one state per source chat; there is no history-length retention.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Monotonic presentation IDs and resource checks serialize ownership logically across overlapping show/promote operations; no task burst or unbounded queue is created.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The promoted chat model is normally warm because the transient card holds a reference. Dismissal clears that reference; subsequent normal reopen may use provider/session caches according to their existing lifecycle.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: cancellation, disposal, host unregister, catalog invalidation, and promotion ownership checks are directly implemented.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The number of simultaneous source groups is environment-dependent, but all retained resources have explicit removal paths.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable cleanup or retention regression.

Scenarios.Scenario: Send an Agent Host side-chat turn with active-agent title generation enabled
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Outgoing contributions run serially before provider send. The new SideChat-origin guard returns before the persisted-title database lookup and rename reminder generation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Open the session database and read persisted title-source metadata
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Previously one serialized lookup per outgoing side-chat turn when active-agent title generation was enabled; now zero for SideChat origins.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The base revision performed the lookup before deciding whether to attach the rename reminder.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Previously blocked turn submission because the contribution dispatcher awaits each onOutgoingTurn hook; now skipped.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Savings scale linearly with side-chat turns.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One ordered contribution pass per outgoing turn; the title step is no longer an awaited I/O operation for side chats.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The old path did not consult an in-memory cache before opening the database for this metadata check; the new origin guard avoids the lookup entirely for side chats.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High; the fixing line and introducing commit were recorded through report_regression_fix.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Database warmth and exact milliseconds vary, but the removed serialized I/O is directly established.
Scenarios.Verdict: This PR fixes a real critical-path latency regression; it is not a review finding against the PR.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 67 changed files. No actionable diff-introduced performance regression met the reporting threshold. The transient path preserves provider-call cardinality, model loads are cached/coalesced and off the send critical path, streaming relayout is frame-coalesced and capped, and cleanup is explicit. One pre-existing side-chat send latency regression fixed by this PR was recorded separately.
